Spotify key metrics — marketplace mix, ARPU, cash, multiple

SPOT-zbar-2026-09-21 · EUR · series 2026-09-23T04:45:00Z · built 2026-09-23 03:57 UTC

The short version

Own SPOT for three to ten years. The business is an audio marketplace with distribution and product at global scale — not a music-rights bet, and not a software multiple waiting for agentic AI to erase headphones. The fear that misprices the stock is that fear applied here. What would change the view first is a sustained slowdown in monthly active users and in listening — not one soft quarter. A second warning would be operating margin falling quarter after quarter without a clear reinvestment story. Podcast and audiobook hours as a share of listening are still blank in the public record; we do not invent them.

SPOT · EUR ops / USD price · as of 2026-09-21 (ET) · CLEAR week ending 2026-09-20

Spotify is not a banner-ad shop waiting for ChatGPT to replace headphones. It is an audio marketplace. It pulls a large global audience into one product, turns that attention into paid subscriptions and into ads on the free tier, and compounds distribution advantages that music rights alone cannot explain.

Two revenue engines share that front door: Premium (paid subscriptions) and Ad-Supported (ads on free). Premium and Ad-Supported users overlap — they are not two pieces of one total. The numbers below are the scoreboard for whether the “software apocalypse” story is earned here.

1. What Spotify is and how it makes money

Spotify Technology S.A. runs a consumer audio platform. Revenue shows up in two engines:

  1. Premium — subscription revenue from paid users.
  2. Ad-Supported — advertising on the free tier.

Premium is still the dollar core. Ad-Supported is the funnel and the smaller absolute line. When the company prints segment totals, Premium plus Ad add to total revenue. User counts are not additive the same way.

In the second quarter of 2026 the company printed €4.78B total revenue, €4.33B Premium, €446M Ad, operating income €655M, and net income €545M. Free cash flow in the quarter was €797M. Survival is not the open question. Audience durability, Premium price and mix, and the margin path are.

Revenue sets the scale; operating margin is the profitability path beside it. Net margin sits on the same chart from the early series through today — including the large net losses of 2018–19 (for example −€394M in the second calendar quarter of 2018, a −31% net margin on that quarter’s revenue).

Fourth-quarter Premium, Ad, revenue, operating income, free cash flow, and ARPU for Q4’18 through Q4’25 are the shareholder-letter prints. Operating income for the first half of 2023 is printed (−€156M and −€247M), so operating margin is −5.13% and −7.77% on those quarters. Early 2018–19 quarters also print net loss attributable to owners (−€169M / −€394M / −€142M / −€76M), so net margin is continuous on that stretch (−14.8% / −31.0% / −9.4% / −4.6%). Q4’22 free cash flow was −€73M and net income −€270M. The fourth quarter of 2021 did not print Ad-Supported monthly active users, so that cell stays blank. Annual Premium ARPU on a full-year stub is a year average — never read it as a fourth-quarter ARPU.

2. Growth engine vs legacy core

Think of the stack as two stories sharing one front door.

Legacy core — Premium. Still the largest dollar engine (Q2’26 Premium €4.33B). Inside it, monetization is carrying through ARPU (€4.89 in Q2’26 versus €4.57 a year earlier) while subscriber year-over-year growth has cooled versus the mid-teens pace of early 2025. That price-and-mix story inside the core is the growth story in the dollars.

Growth / funnel — Ad-Supported users and Ad revenue. Ad-Supported monthly active users grew +14.1% year over year to 494M in Q2’26, faster than Premium’s +8.7% to 300M. Ad revenue itself printed €446M, a touch soft versus €453M a year earlier — so the funnel is still expanding while the free-tier dollar print is the softer watch item this quarter.

Podcasts and audiobooks are thesis color. Hours and share of listening are null in every period we checked. That is a narrative gap, not a chart we fake.

3a. Audience

Second-quarter 2026: 777M monthly active users, 300M Premium, 494M Ad-Supported, versus 696 / 276 / 433 a year earlier. Year over year that is +11.6% / +8.7% / +14.1%. Quarter over quarter net adds were +16M / +7M / +11M.

Monthly-active-user growth has sat in a roughly eleven-to-twelve percent band for eight quarters — seasonal noise and a soft comparison, not a sustained audience collapse. Premium growth has slowed versus the first half of 2025; Ad is the faster top of funnel. That wedge is the live tension for a long-only holder.

Premium divided by monthly active users is ~38.6%. That is stock mix, not conversion. True free-to-paid conversion stays off this page.

3b. Premium core — ARPU carrying the dollars

Premium ARPU printed €4.89 in Q2’26 (Q1 €4.76; Q2’25 €4.57). Premium revenue €4.33B versus €3.74B a year earlier. Price and mix are doing work on the paid side while subscriber year-over-year decelerates. Q4’25 letter ARPU printed €4.70. A year-average ARPU on a full-year stub is not a fourth-quarter ARPU.

3c. Ad-Supported — funnel up, dollars watched

Ad-Supported monthly active users are the cleaner growth line on the user scoreboard. Ad revenue remains a smaller absolute line and was slightly down year over year in Q2’26. The fourth quarter of 2021 did not print Ad-Supported users, so that bar — and the Ad year-over-year rates that depend on it — stay blank. Do not paper over that with podcast-hour claims the record does not have.

3d. Optional geo color

Annual monthly-active-user mix by region (Europe / Latin America / North America / Rest of World) from FY2018–FY2025 is shares of one audience — Rest of World has been the rising share. No quarterly geo, no geo Premium, no geo ARPU in the record we use.

4. Unit economics → valuation

For this pack the hierarchy is simple:

  1. Premium ARPU — price and mix without inventing conversion.
  2. Operating margin path — watch sustained quarter-over-quarter decline, not one step.
  3. Free cash flow — quarterly bars, including letter fourth quarters.
  4. Weekly trailing multiple, with street forward shown as a dotted projection on the same chart — honest blanks where the estimate file is empty.

Trailing four quarters of free cash flow (Q3’25–Q2’26, including Q4’25 €834M) sum to roughly €3.26B. FY2025 free cash flow was €2.87B; FY2024 €2.29B.

Cash on the quarterly balance sheet is sparse. We do not invent quarterly cash.
